market_context.summary: The organising fact is the long end: the 10Y sits at 5.24% against a 3.88% effective funds rate, with 10y-2y at +0.42 — a steep, term-premium curve rather than a growth one. Oil in the low-to-mid $90s supplies the inflation impulse behind that term premium, and the event markets agree: Kalshi prices September CPI accelerating from 3.4% to roughly 3.6% and a 74% chance of a 25bp Fed HIKE on 2026-12-09, with ~1c on any cut at either remaining meeting. The easing cycle is priced as over and reversing. That single fact sorts the tape: a tailwind for bank and insurer net interest margin, a headwind for long duration (TLT 78.37) and for rate-sensitive cyclicals. Sector dispersion is extreme and does not net out to a single risk setting — energy producers and refiners are at 120-day highs (XLE 67.20, XOM 174.08) while oil services are in a bear market at the same time (SLB -19.3%, HAL -24.8% off their highs), and aerospace/defense is ~18.2% off its 2026-08-14 record on a budget-timing cause rather than a demand one. SPY closed 778.01, essentially flat. Stated plainly: there is no index or VIX reading in this report at all — every index source failed — so 'mixed' is a read of sector internals and the rate complex, not of a volatility level I was able to measure.

recommendations.counter_argument: Four misses of 0.5%, 0.5%, 10.2% and 17.4% are not four equal misses - two of them are rounding, and the two large ones are the oldest two, so the trend within the misses is actually of the company closing the gap, not widening it. Combined with a 45.7% six-month underperformance already banked, the strongest bear-case-against is simply that the de-rating has already happened and the 10-20 print is as likely to mark the bottom as extend the fall. That is why the entry is a bounce and not the close, and why the idea is abandoned outright if the bounce does not arrive. RED TEAM: conviction lowered 4 -> 3 and the target pulled in from 64.00 to 65.50. Two of the three evidence kinds are weaker than they read. The thesis headline is 'four consecutive misses', but this counter_argument already concedes two of them are rounding and the two large ones are the oldest — so the series supports 'the street has roughly caught up', not 'the street has not finished cutting', which is the claim the short is actually underwritten on. And the `positioning` kind cites a bullish share of 74.1%: that is still an overwhelming bull consensus, and 'down 3.5 points' from it is not a deteriorating-revisions signal. On the target, the validator flagged 64.00 as 6.19 ATR away, past the 6.0 guide, and it sat below the 65.08 range low — 65.50 is 5.16 ATR and inside measured structure. Reward-to-risk falls 2.90 -> 2.42 as a result, which still clears the floor; the ratio got worse because the level got honest. data_quality_notes:
RESEARCH COMPLETE — the notes carry both a completion block and a 06:40 addendum, so nothing here was lost to the clock. Seven candidates were captured and all seven are published; four were rejected on their merits during research (WDC, VLO, OXY, TLT) and the count is what it is because the bar was raised, not because the lane was filled.

WHAT THIS REPORT CANNOT SEE: September CPI prints TODAY at 08:30 ET, about two hours after publication. No price, level or ratio anywhere in this report reflects it, and it is the single most consequential fact of the morning — the market prices an acceleration from 3.4% to roughly 3.6%. It is named first in the key_risk of both rate-path ideas (XLF, TRV) for that reason. TRV's entry instruction was changed from a resting order to 'let the print clear first'.

PRICES: every quote is the 2026-10-13 regular-session close (asof 20:00 UTC), refetched at synthesis and unchanged. The market was shut at generation, so the previous close is the freshest honest price available — that is a closed market, not stale data.

SOURCES THAT FAILED: no index level anywhere and NO VIX READING AT ALL — ^GSPC, ^NDX, ^DJI, ^RUT and ^VIX failed on every source (finnhub needs a CFD subscription, yahoo returned HTTP 429, stooq 404). No crypto prices (CoinGecko), so no crypto idea could be priced or stopped. No futures (ES, NQ), DXY, gold or WTI quotes; the oil figure used for context came from undated third-party tickers disagreeing by ~$3 and is described only as 'low-to-mid $90s' rather than quoted. No options-implied move for any idea (yahoo-options returns HTTP 401 on every call), so the 'is your target inside what the market prices' check could not be run once today. No short interest or days-to-cover for any name (api.nasdaq.com timed out) — this is the main unquantified risk in the NFLX short, where squeeze risk is the thing most likely to break it, and it is stated as unmeasured in that idea's key_risk rather than glossed.

EVENT CONTRACTS ARE NOT A GAP. `market_data.py events` returns ok:true with count 0, but the Kalshi API queried directly returns live, deep markets (OI 122k on the CPI 3.6% strike, 1.58M on the October hold, quoted 1-4c wide). The correct statement is 'event contracts available, no defensible edge found': there is no independent September CPI estimate behind any view I could take, and fading a deep, tightly-quoted market two hours before resolution on 'oil is high so CPI runs hot' is the hunch config/universe.md forbids — the market has already priced that reasoning. The wrapper bug is worth fixing; the absence of an event trade today is a judgement, not an outage.

ARITHMETIC: every reward-to-risk ratio and stop distance was recomputed at synthesis from the refetched quotes and ATR14 values, not carried over from the candidate files. All seven matched and all seven clear both floors. Conviction scores were checked against distinct evidence kinds and all seven are exact (HII 5 on 4 kinds; XLF, TRV, NFLX, VICR 4 on 3; STLD, GE 3 on 2).

RATIOS TO BE SUSPICIOUS OF: four of the six swing ideas land within 0.12 of the 2.0 floor — VICR 2.00, GE 2.06, TRV 2.07, STLD 2.12. That clustering is the signature of targets fitted to clear the bar, so it is flagged rather than left for the reader to notice. The mitigating evidence is the other side of the same test: every stop sits 2.17-2.58 ATR from entry, comfortably above its floor, so these ratios were not manufactured by walking a stop inward — the notes record that VICR was left at exactly 2.00 rather than trimmed to a 230 stop to manufacture 2.3. The honest reading is that the targets are capped by real overhead structure, which is the right place for them to be capped, and that four of these ideas have very little margin for error.

SKEW, AND WHY: 6 swing, 1 long_term, 0 intraday. Nothing intraday was published because every equity price available at 06:00 ET is the previous close, and setting the precise intraday levels config/strategy.md requires off a previous close would be inventing them. 6 stock, 1 ETF, 0 crypto, 0 futures, 0 event contracts — the first two of those are the source outages above, the third is the judgement above. Only one long-term idea, and it is an update rather than a new thesis; the lane is not neglected (CCJ, BCC and PFE are open long-term positions, all reviewed, none changed) and the two new long-term theses worked up both failed on evidence (WDC on valuation, oil services on sourcing) rather than on time.

NEW RISK VERSUS POSITION MANAGEMENT: of the seven, four are updates or re-pitches of lines already tracked — XLF (hold, levels unchanged), GE (hold, levels unchanged, one input got worse), HII (pacing update, zone and target unchanged), STLD (unfilled stop-limit re-pitched at unchanged levels). Three are genuinely new: TRV, the NFLX short, and VICR. Eleven other open positions were triaged and none re-captured, because an unchanged position with nothing new to say is not an idea. DINO hit its 128.00 target on 2026-10-13 and grades as a win; it is not re-pitched.

TWO IDEAS ARE MARKED WAIT and are held out of performance tracking until they trigger: NFLX is the bounce into 72.50-73.50 or it is nothing, and STLD only participates if the base resolves upward through 245.185.

TIMING CORRELATION, WHICH THE DRIVER CAP DOES NOT CATCH: no single driver carries more than two ideas (rate path 2: XLF, TRV — the third slot deliberately left empty rather than spent on the thin TLT short). But GE, STLD, VICR and NFLX all resolve on prints inside 2026-10-19 to 10-20, so while their theses are independent their timing is not; a bad tape that week marks four of seven at once.

TRACK RECORD APPLIED: the report is 2/18 to target overall and 0/11 on single stocks. The sample is still under the ~15 closed trades at which a by-category read stops being noise, so no category was cut outright; the response was a higher bar, giving four worked-up rejections against seven captures.

UNEXPLAINED AND MISLEADING MOVES, RECORDED RATHER THAN ATTRIBUTED: DINO +4.3% and SMMT -9.4% on 2026-10-13 both lack a sourced cause — no 8-K, no same-day report found for either — so they are logged as unexplained rather than attributed to a mechanism I did not fetch. Separately, HON shows -56.8% off its 120-day high and that is a corporate action, not a de-rating: the 'high' is pre-separation Honeywell. Anything screening on pct_off_high will surface it as the cheapest large cap on the board. NFLX's 94.70 -> 70.46 range, by contrast, is post-split pricing throughout and is a real -25.6% de-rating.

ONE ACTION IS NOT A RECOMMENDATION BUT NEEDS DOING THIS MORNING: cancel the resting KXCPIYOY-26SEP-T3.5 NO @ 18 order before 08:30 ET. See the watchlist.

MECHANICAL VALIDATION, AND A VERIFIER BUG FOUND WHILE RUNNING IT: the validator independently recomputed all seven reward-to-risk ratios from live prices and ATR14 and every one matched what is published (claimed -> computed identical on all seven), which is the check that matters most here. It also reported all seven ideas' sources as returning 404 — and that was wrong. `check_sources` probed with HEAD only, and both `api.nasdaq.com/api/quote/<sym>/historical` and the Kalshi markets endpoint route only GET, answering HEAD with a 404 rather than the 405 that would say so. Both are real endpoints this report fetches every morning; a GET returns 200. Left alone, the `--enforce` step would have demoted all seven ideas to the watchlist and published nothing, on a probe error rather than a data problem. The probe now confirms a HEAD 404 with a streamed GET before calling a URL invented, with tests in `tests/test_validate_report.py`. Six of the seven verdicts went from fail to warn as a result. The sources themselves were not changed — substituting friendlier URLs to satisfy a broken probe would have hidden the bug and weakened the provenance.

ONE GENUINE VALIDATION FAILURE REMAINS, AND IT IS NOT BEING PAPERED OVER: STLD fails on a measured bid/ask spread of 6.95%, a round trip costing 48% of the target move. That is a real number, not a probe artifact, and it is read off a closed-market book — a $227M-a-day name would not show 7% in regular hours. But STLD's entry is a resting stop-limit trigger, so book quality is exactly what the idea depends on, and the red team should either confirm the spread in regular hours or let the demotion stand. Published at rank 6 with the flag attached rather than quietly dropped or quietly kept.

ONE VALIDATION WARNING IS A KNOWN ARTIFACT: 'claims an earnings catalyst but <symbol> is not on the fetched calendar' fires on six ideas. For XLF it is simply correct and not a defect — an ETF has no earnings, and its catalyst is the bank reporting wave plus today's CPI, not XLF's own print. For NFLX, TRV, VICR, STLD and GE the dates were confirmed against the finnhub earnings calendar during research and re-confirmed in the candidate records; the validator's own calendar fetch covers a shorter forward window than the dates cited. Worth fixing in the check, but it is not evidence the dates are wrong.

Note for the pipeline, not the reader: the test suite has 7 pre-existing failures in `tests/test_tax_deed_screen.py`, unrelated to this report — the tax-deed fixtures are pinned to a 2026-10-06 sale date that has now passed, so every fixture listing is rejected as `sale_date_passed`. Present before today's change and untouched by it.

RED TEAM (phase 2c, 06:45-07:05 ET): cut 2 of 7, downgraded 4, fixed 1 level, 5 remain.

CUT. VICR (was rank 5) — the thesis names its own edge mechanism, 'the street cannot model this company', and the idea's own counter_argument retires it with a number: consensus went from 0.1428 to 1.03, a bar seven times higher than the one the 341% beat cleared. A 6.7-point claimed edge needs a live mechanism. R:R exactly 2.00 and a single reversal bar on a 7.25%-ATR name compound it. STLD (was rank 6) — the 2.12 R:R is computed off a stop-limit trigger the order cannot guarantee: STLD reports 10-19 AMC, so a trigger 2.0% above the close most likely fires on the 10-20 opening gap, which its own key_risk concedes.

THE STLD SPREAD WAS CHECKED AS THE REPORT ASKED, AND THE REPORT'S ASSUMPTION WAS WRONG. It called the 6.95% a closed-market artifact. Regular hours were unreachable at 06:44 ET, but the same Nasdaq endpoint in the same minute returned AAPL 0.035% and MSFT 0.118% against STLD's bid 228.55 / ask 245.00, flagged is_real_time — so the feed is sound and the wide book is this name's. It is a live pre-market book, not a closed one, and that session is exactly where this order expects to fill. The flag is measured in the wrong session for a routine fill and the right one for this one. The validation fail stands rather than being argued away.

DOWNGRADED. HII 5 -> 4: of four evidence kinds, counter_argument_answered says in its own text 'Answered partially, not fully', and the 430 target is this report's margin assumption rather than anything a source states. NFLX 4 -> 3: the 'four consecutive misses' headline is conceded by its own counter to be two rounding misses plus two older large ones, which supports 'the street has caught up' rather than 'has not finished cutting'; and a 74.1% bullish share is a bull consensus, not a short signal. TRV 4 -> 3: the third kind, technical_level, is where the stop went rather than independent corroboration. GE 3 -> 2: expectancy +0.10R on a 3.3-point edge, two kinds of which one is just the earnings date, on a chart the report itself calls broken.

GE IS DOWNGRADED, NOT CUT, AND THE DISTINCTION IS DELIBERATE. It was filled at 308.00 on 10-12, so the entry is a price already paid; demoting a filled line to the watchlist would read as a sell instruction the levels do not support. The 292.00 stop and the trim-into-the-open plan carry it.

VALIDATOR ARTIFACT CONFIRMED AS AN ARTIFACT. The 'not on the fetched calendar' warn fired on six ideas. An independent finnhub pull at 06:44 ET returned all five equity dates exactly as published — NFLX 10-20 amc, VICR 10-20 bmo, GE 10-19 bmo, STLD 10-19 amc, TRV 10-16 bmo, EPS estimates matching to four decimals. CORRELATION, AFTER THE CUTS. Removing VICR and STLD dissolves the 10-19/10-20 industrial-print cluster that had four of seven ideas resolving inside two sessions; GE is the only survivor of it. What remains is the rate-path pair, and the overlap is closer than the driver cap sees: Travelers is a component of XLF, so XLF at 3% plus TRV at 2.5% is 5.5% of the book long financials on one rate path, sharing today's 08:30 CPI as the first-named risk of both. Both are kept — XLF is filled with its catalyst arriving today, and TRV is now gated behind 10-16 — but they should be sized as nearer to one position than two. TLT's watchlist trigger asks for 'the retirement of one of the two financials'; neither retired, so TLT stays out.

WHAT WAS NOT CUT, AND WHY NOT. XLF came through untouched. It is the only idea whose three evidence kinds are genuinely independent and all externally sourced — dated bank-reporting calendar, a Kalshi rate path with 138k-1.58M open interest rather than an assumption, and a reclaimed 20-day — and its counter_argument already states the bounce-within-a-downtrend problem without being prompted. Manufacturing an objection to it would be the harm this phase is warned against.

RED TEAM, SECOND PASS — re-running validation after the first pass surfaced two fails and one stale field, so 3 of the original 7 are now cut and 4 survive.

TRV CUT (was rank 4). Four counts had already accumulated against the trade while the thesis stayed sound, and re-validation added a fifth that I am explicitly NOT leaning on. The deciding ones: the 366-372 zone is already behind the market (closed 373.28, pre-market ask 378.50), so a resting order was unfillable; the 10-16 catalyst turns on a Q3 catastrophe-loss figure this report could not fetch; the sell-side and insider picture is uniformly negative into a target set at the prior range high; and TRV is a component of XLF, so the pair was 5.5% of book on one rate path. Validation separately returned a live 6.25% pre-market spread — an 83% round trip — and that flag genuinely does NOT describe this order's fill, because a gated regular-hours limit on a Dow component trades pennies wide where STLD's stop-limit was built to fire into an opening gap. Stating that distinction rather than quietly banking the fail, because treating two spread flags differently is exactly where motivated reasoning would hide. The structural reinvestment-yield thesis is kept on the watchlist with a post-print trigger.

GE TRIMMED 2.5% -> 1%, not just downgraded. Conviction 2 carries a 1% lottery-ticket ceiling, and validation failed the position on it — correctly. Leaving 2.5% on would have been the downgrade without its consequence. The line is flat (filled 308.00 on 10-12, last 307.63), so the trim is free and is taken before the 10-19 print rather than after it. Still not demoted to the watchlist: the entry is a price already paid.

NFLX risk_reward corrected 2.9 -> 2.42, which was my own stale field after pulling the target in from 64.00 to 65.50. The validator caught the mismatch between the claim and the numbers, which is the check working on the red team rather than on the author.

CORRELATION, FINAL. Of the four ideas resolving inside 10-19/10-20 that the research phase flagged as a timing cluster, only GE remains, now at 1%. Financials exposure is XLF alone at 3%. TLT's watchlist trigger asked for 'the retirement of one of the two financials' and that slot is now free — TLT is still not taken, because R:R at exactly 2.00 with a target above the range low was never only a correlation problem, and a freed slot is not a reason to fill it.

NET OF BOTH PASSES: 3 cut (VICR, STLD, TRV), 4 downgraded (HII 5->4, NFLX 4->3, TRV 4->3 before being cut, GE 3->2), 1 target pulled inward, 1 position trimmed, 1 missing entry condition written in, 1 claimed ratio corrected. Four recommendations survive: HII, XLF, NFLX, GE. Gross exposure falls from 18% to 10%. XLF was not touched in either pass and that is a finding, not an omission — it is the only idea whose three evidence kinds are independent and all externally sourced.
